paragraphs.text: Now when morning was come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death:
paragraphs.original: Πρωΐας δὲ γενομένης συμβούλιον ἔλαβον πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὥστε θανατῶσαι αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: Prōias de genomenēs symboulion elabon pantes hoi archiereis kai hoi presbyteroi tou laou kata tou Iēsou hōste thanatōsai auton·

paragraphs.text: and they bound him, and led him away, and delivered him up to Pilate the governor.
paragraphs.original: καὶ δήσαντες αὐτὸν ἀπήγαγον καὶ παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ τῷ ἡγεμόνι.
paragraphs.translit: kai dēsantes auton apēgagon kai paredōkan Pilatō tō hēgemoni.

paragraphs.text: Then Judas, who betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
paragraphs.original: Τότε ἰδὼν Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ὅτι κατεκρίθη μεταμεληθεὶς ἔστρεψεν τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ πρεσβυτέροις
paragraphs.translit: Tote idōn Ioudas ho paradidous auton hoti katekrithē metamelētheis estrepsen ta triakonta argyria tois archiereusin kai presbyterois

paragraphs.text: saying, I have sinned in that I betrayed innocent blood. But they said, What is that to us? see thou [to it].
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Ἥμαρτον παραδοὺς αἷμα ἀθῷον. οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς; σὺ ὄψῃ.
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Hēmarton paradous haima athōon. hoi de eipan· Ti pros hēmas; sy opsē.

paragraphs.text: And he cast down the pieces of silver into the sanctuary, and departed; and he went away and hanged himself.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ῥίψας τὰ ἀργύρια εἰς τὸν ναὸν ἀνεχώρησεν, καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπήγξατο.
paragraphs.translit: kai rhipsas ta argyria eis ton naon anechōrēsen, kai apelthōn apēnxato.

paragraphs.text: And the chief priests took the pieces of silver, and said, It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is the price of blood.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἔξεστιν βαλεῖν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν κορβανᾶν, ἐπεὶ τιμὴ αἵματός ἐστιν·
paragraphs.translit: hoi de archiereis labontes ta argyria eipan· Ouk exestin balein auta eis ton korbanan, epei timē haimatos estin·

paragraphs.text: And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter`s field, to bury strangers in.
paragraphs.original: συμβούλιον δὲ λαβόντες ἠγόρασαν ἐξ αὐτῶν τὸν Ἀγρὸν τοῦ Κεραμέως εἰς ταφὴν τοῖς ξένοις.
paragraphs.translit: symboulion de labontes ēgorasan ex autōn ton Agron tou Kerameōs eis taphēn tois xenois.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore that field was called, the field of blood, unto this day.
paragraphs.original: διὸ ἐκλήθη ὁ ἀγρὸς ἐκεῖνος Ἀγρὸς Αἵματος ἕως τῆς σήμερον.
paragraphs.translit: dio eklēthē ho agros ekeinos Agros Haimatos heōs tēs sēmeron.

paragraphs.text: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was priced, whom [certain] of the children of Israel did price;
paragraphs.original: τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἰερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Καὶ ἔλαβον τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια, τὴν τιμὴν τοῦ τετιμημένου ὃν ἐτιμήσαντο ἀπὸ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ,
paragraphs.translit: tote eplērōthē to rhēthen dia Ieremiou tou prophētou legontos· Kai elabon ta triakonta argyria, tēn timēn tou tetimēmenou hon etimēsanto apo hyiōn Israēl,

paragraphs.text: and they gave them for the potter`s field, as the Lord appointed me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔδωκαν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν τοῦ κεραμέως, καθὰ συνέταξέν μοι κύριος.
paragraphs.translit: kai edōkan auta eis ton agron tou kerameōs, katha synetaxen moi kyrios.

paragraphs.text: Now Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐστάθη ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ἡγεμόνος· καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ ἡγεμὼν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.
paragraphs.translit: Ho de Iēsous estathē emprosthen tou hēgemonos· kai epērōtēsen auton ho hēgemōn legōn· Sy ei ho basileus tōn Ioudaiōn; ho de Iēsous ephē· Sy legeis.

paragraphs.text: And when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ κατηγορεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο.
paragraphs.translit: kai en tō katēgoreisthai auton hypo tōn archiereōn kai presbyterōn ouden apekrinato.

paragraphs.text: Then saith Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee?
paragraphs.original: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Οὐκ ἀκούεις πόσα σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;
paragraphs.translit: tote legei autō ho Pilatos· Ouk akoueis posa sou katamartyrousin;

paragraphs.text: And he gave him no answer, not even to one word: insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ πρὸς οὐδὲ ἓν ῥῆμα, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν ἡγεμόνα λίαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk apekrithē autō pros oude hen rhēma, hōste thaumazein ton hēgemona lian.

paragraphs.text: Now at the feast the governor was wont to release unto the multitude one prisoner, whom they would.
paragraphs.original: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν εἰώθει ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἀπολύειν ἕνα τῷ ὄχλῳ δέσμιον ὃν ἤθελον.
paragraphs.translit: Kata de heortēn eiōthei ho hēgemōn apolyein hena tō ochlō desmion hon ēthelon.

paragraphs.text: And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas.
paragraphs.original: εἶχον δὲ τότε δέσμιον ἐπίσημον λεγόμενον Ἰησοῦν Βαραββᾶν.
paragraphs.translit: eichon de tote desmion episēmon legomenon Iēsoun Barabban.

paragraphs.text: When therefore they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?
paragraphs.original: συνηγμένων οὖν αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν, Ἰησοῦν τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἢ Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν;
paragraphs.translit: synēgmenōn oun autōn eipen autois ho Pilatos· Tina thelete apolysō hymin, Iēsoun ton Barabban ē Iēsoun ton legomenon christon;

paragraphs.text: For he knew that for envy they had delivered him up.
paragraphs.original: ᾔδει γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παρέδωκαν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ēdei gar hoti dia phthonon paredōkan auton.

paragraphs.text: And while he was sitting on the judgment-seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that righteous man; for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
paragraphs.original: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ λέγουσα· Μηδὲν σοὶ καὶ τῷ δικαίῳ ἐκείνῳ, πολλὰ γὰρ ἔπαθον σήμερον κατʼ ὄναρ διʼ αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kathēmenou de autou epi tou bēmatos apesteilen pros auton hē gynē autou legousa· Mēden soi kai tō dikaiō ekeinō, polla gar epathon sēmeron katʼ onar diʼ auton.

paragraphs.text: Now the chief priests and the elders persuaded the multitudes that they should ask for Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεισαν τοὺς ὄχλους ἵνα αἰτήσωνται τὸν Βαραββᾶν τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν ἀπολέσωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi de archiereis kai hoi presbyteroi epeisan tous ochlous hina aitēsōntai ton Barabban ton de Iēsoun apolesōsin.

paragraphs.text: But the governor answered and said unto them, Which of the two will ye that I release unto you? And they said, Barabbas.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἡγεμὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπὸ τῶν δύο ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τὸν Βαραββᾶν.
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho hēgemōn eipen autois· Tina thelete apo tōn dyo apolysō hymin; hoi de eipan· Ton Barabban.

paragraphs.text: Pilate saith unto them, What then shall I do unto Jesus who is called Christ? They all say, Let him be crucified.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τί οὖν ποιήσω Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν; λέγουσιν πάντες· Σταυρωθήτω.
paragraphs.translit: legei autois ho Pilatos· Ti oun poiēsō Iēsoun ton legomenon christon; legousin pantes· Staurōthētō.

paragraphs.text: And he said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out exceedingly, saying, Let him be crucified.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν; οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Σταυρωθήτω.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ephē· Ti gar kakon epoiēsen; hoi de perissōs ekrazon legontes· Staurōthētō.

paragraphs.text: So when Pilate saw that he prevailed nothing, but rather that a tumult was arising, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; see ye [to it].
paragraphs.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ὅτι οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον θόρυβος γίνεται λαβὼν ὕδωρ ἀπενίψατο τὰς χεῖρας ἀπέναντι τοῦ ὄχλου λέγων· Ἀθῷός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος τούτου· ὑμεῖς ὄψεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: Idōn de ho Pilatos hoti ouden ōphelei alla mallon thorybos ginetai labōn hydōr apenipsato tas cheiras apenanti tou ochlou legōn· Athōos eimi apo tou haimatos toutou· hymeis opsesthe.

paragraphs.text: And all the people answered and said, His blood [be] on us, and on our children.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πᾶς ὁ λαὸς εἶπεν· Τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis pas ho laos eipen· To haima autou ephʼ hēmas kai epi ta tekna hēmōn.

paragraphs.text: Then released he unto them Barabbas; but Jesus he scourged and delivered to be crucified.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας παρέδωκεν ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.
paragraphs.translit: tote apelysen autois ton Barabban, ton de Iēsoun phragellōsas paredōken hina staurōthē.

paragraphs.text: Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the Praetorium, and gathered unto him the whole band.
paragraphs.original: Τότε οἱ στρατιῶται τοῦ ἡγεμόνος παραλαβόντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον συνήγαγον ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.
paragraphs.translit: Tote hoi stratiōtai tou hēgemonos paralabontes ton Iēsoun eis to praitōrion synēgagon epʼ auton holēn tēn speiran.

paragraphs.text: And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν χλαμύδα κοκκίνην περιέθηκαν αὐτῷ,
paragraphs.translit: kai ekdysantes auton chlamyda kokkinēn periethēkan autō,

paragraphs.text: And they platted a crown of thorns and put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand; and they kneeled down before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews!
paragraphs.original: καὶ πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ κάλαμον ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ γονυπετήσαντες ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Χαῖρε, βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων,
paragraphs.translit: kai plexantes stephanon ex akanthōn epethēkan epi tēs kephalēs autou kai kalamon en tē dexia autou, kai gonypetēsantes emprosthen autou enepaixan autō legontes· Chaire, basileu tōn Ioudaiōn,

paragraphs.text: And they spat upon him, and took the reed and smote him on the head.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐμπτύσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν ἔλαβον τὸν κάλαμον καὶ ἔτυπτον εἰς τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai emptysantes eis auton elabon ton kalamon kai etypton eis tēn kephalēn autou.

paragraphs.text: And when they had mocked him, they took off from him the robe, and put on him his garments, and led him away to crucify him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν χλαμύδα καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σταυρῶσαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai hote enepaixan autō, exedysan auton tēn chlamyda kai enedysan auton ta himatia autou kai apēgagon auton eis to staurōsai.

paragraphs.text: And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they compelled to go [with them], that he might bear his cross.
paragraphs.original: Ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ εὗρον ἄνθρωπον Κυρηναῖον ὀνόματι Σίμωνα· τοῦτον ἠγγάρευσαν ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Exerchomenoi de heuron anthrōpon Kyrēnaion onomati Simōna· touton ēngareusan hina arē ton stauron autou.

paragraphs.text: And they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, The place of a skull,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Γολγοθᾶ, ὅ ἐστιν Κρανίου Τόπος λεγόμενος,
paragraphs.translit: Kai elthontes eis topon legomenon Golgotha, ho estin Kraniou Topos legomenos,

paragraphs.text: they gave him wine to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted it, he would not drink.
paragraphs.original: ἔδωκαν αὐτῷ πιεῖν οἶνον μετὰ χολῆς μεμιγμένον· καὶ γευσάμενος οὐκ ἠθέλησεν πιεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: edōkan autō piein oinon meta cholēs memigmenon· kai geusamenos ouk ēthelēsen piein.

paragraphs.text: And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments among them, casting lots;
paragraphs.original: σταυρώσαντες δὲ αὐτὸν διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ βάλλοντες κλῆρον,
paragraphs.translit: staurōsantes de auton diemerisanto ta himatia autou ballontes klēron,

paragraphs.text: and they sat and watched him there.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθήμενοι ἐτήρουν αὐτὸν ἐκεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: kai kathēmenoi etēroun auton ekei.

paragraphs.text: And they set up over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπάνω τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ τὴν αἰτίαν αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένην· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
paragraphs.translit: kai epethēkan epanō tēs kephalēs autou tēn aitian autou gegrammenēn· Houtos estin Iēsous ho basileus tōn Ioudaiōn.

paragraphs.text: Then are there crucified with him two robbers, one on the right hand and one on the left.
paragraphs.original: Τότε σταυροῦνται σὺν αὐτῷ δύο λῃσταί, εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων.
paragraphs.translit: Tote staurountai syn autō dyo lēstai, heis ek dexiōn kai heis ex euōnymōn.

paragraphs.text: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads,
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν
paragraphs.translit: hoi de paraporeuomenoi eblasphēmoun auton kinountes tas kephalas autōn

paragraphs.text: and saying, Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself: if thou art the Son of God, come down from the cross.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγοντες· Ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις οἰκοδομῶν, σῶσον σεαυτόν· εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, κατάβηθι ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai legontes· Ho katalyōn ton naon kai en trisin hēmerais oikodomōn, sōson seauton· ei hyios ei tou theou, katabēthi apo tou staurou.

paragraphs.text: In like manner also the chief priests mocking [him], with the scribes and elders, said,
paragraphs.original: ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων ἔλεγον·
paragraphs.translit: homoiōs kai hoi archiereis empaizontes meta tōn grammateōn kai presbyterōn elegon·

paragraphs.text: He saved others; himself he cannot save. He is the King of Israel; let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe on him.
paragraphs.original: Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι· βασιλεὺς Ἰσραήλ ἐστιν, καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ καὶ πιστεύσομεν ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Allous esōsen, heauton ou dynatai sōsai· basileus Israēl estin, katabatō nyn apo tou staurou kai pisteusomen epʼ auton.

paragraphs.text: He trusteth on God; let him deliver him now, if he desireth him: for he said, I am the Son of God.
paragraphs.original: πέποιθεν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ῥυσάσθω νῦν εἰ θέλει αὐτόν· εἶπεν γὰρ ὅτι Θεοῦ εἰμι υἱός.
paragraphs.translit: pepoithen epi ton theon, rhysasthō nyn ei thelei auton· eipen gar hoti Theou eimi hyios.

paragraphs.text: And the robbers also that were crucified with him cast upon him the same reproach.
paragraphs.original: τὸ δʼ αὐτὸ καὶ οἱ λῃσταὶ οἱ συσταυρωθέντες σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: to dʼ auto kai hoi lēstai hoi systaurōthentes syn autō ōneidizon auton.

paragraphs.text: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land until the ninth hour.
paragraphs.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ ἕκτης ὥρας σκότος ἐγένετο ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.
paragraphs.translit: Apo de hektēs hōras skotos egeneto epi pasan tēn gēn heōs hōras enatēs.

paragraphs.text: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
paragraphs.original: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἐνάτην ὥραν ἀνεβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγων· Ἠλὶ ἠλὶ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι; τοῦτʼ ἔστιν· Θεέ μου θεέ μου, ἱνατί με ἐγκατέλιπες;
paragraphs.translit: peri de tēn enatēn hōran aneboēsen ho Iēsous phōnē megalē legōn· Ēli ēli lema sabachthani; toutʼ estin· Thee mou thee mou, hinati me enkatelipes;

paragraphs.text: And some of them stood there, when they heard it, said, This man calleth Elijah.
paragraphs.original: τινὲς δὲ τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ οὗτος.
paragraphs.translit: tines de tōn ekei hestēkotōn akousantes elegon hoti Ēlian phōnei houtos.

paragraphs.text: And straightway one of them ran, and took a sponge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθέως δραμὼν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν καὶ λαβὼν σπόγγον πλήσας τε ὄξους καὶ περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eutheōs dramōn heis ex autōn kai labōn spongon plēsas te oxous kai peritheis kalamō epotizen auton.

paragraphs.text: And the rest said, Let be; let us see whether Elijah cometh to save him.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἔλεγον· Ἄφες ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας σώσων αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de loipoi elegon· Aphes idōmen ei erchetai Ēlias sōsōn auton.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus cried again with a loud voice, and yielded up his spirit.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἀφῆκεν τὸ πνεῦμα.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous palin kraxas phōnē megalē aphēken to pneuma.

paragraphs.text: And behold, the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake; and the rocks were rent;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη ἀπʼ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω εἰς δύο, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐσείσθη, καὶ αἱ πέτραι ἐσχίσθησαν,
paragraphs.translit: kai idou to katapetasma tou naou eschisthē apʼ anōthen heōs katō eis dyo, kai hē gē eseisthē, kai hai petrai eschisthēsan,

paragraphs.text: and the tombs were opened; and many bodies of the saints that had fallen asleep were raised;
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὰ μνημεῖα ἀνεῴχθησαν καὶ πολλὰ σώματα τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἁγίων ἠγέρθησαν,
paragraphs.translit: kai ta mnēmeia aneōchthēsan kai polla sōmata tōn kekoimēmenōn hagiōn ēgerthēsan,

paragraphs.text: and coming forth out of the tombs after his resurrection they entered into the holy city and appeared unto many.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκ τῶν μνημείων μετὰ τὴν ἔγερσιν αὐτοῦ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν καὶ ἐνεφανίσθησαν πολλοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthontes ek tōn mnēmeiōn meta tēn egersin autou eisēlthon eis tēn hagian polin kai enephanisthēsan pollois.

paragraphs.text: Now the centurion, and they that were with him watching Jesus, when they saw the earthquake, and the things that were done, feared exceedingly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ δὲ ἑκατόνταρχος καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ τηροῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδόντες τὸν σεισμὸν καὶ τὰ γενόμενα ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς ἦν οὗτος.
paragraphs.translit: Ho de hekatontarchos kai hoi metʼ autou tērountes ton Iēsoun idontes ton seismon kai ta genomena ephobēthēsan sphodra legontes· Alēthōs theou hyios ēn houtos.

paragraphs.text: And many women were there beholding from afar, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him:
paragraphs.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ γυναῖκες πολλαὶ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, αἵτινες ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας διακονοῦσαι αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: Ēsan de ekei gynaikes pollai apo makrothen theōrousai, haitines ēkolouthēsan tō Iēsou apo tēs Galilaias diakonousai autō·

paragraphs.text: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
paragraphs.original: ἐν αἷς ἦν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσὴφ μήτηρ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου.
paragraphs.translit: en hais ēn Maria hē Magdalēnē kai Maria hē tou Iakōbou kai Iōsēph mētēr kai hē mētēr tōn hyiōn Zebedaiou.

paragraphs.text: And when even was come, there came a rich man from Arimathaea, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus` disciple:
paragraphs.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἦλθεν ἄνθρωπος πλούσιος ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας, τοὔνομα Ἰωσήφ, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐμαθητεύθη τῷ Ἰησοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Opsias de genomenēs ēlthen anthrōpos plousios apo Harimathaias, tounoma Iōsēph, hos kai autos emathēteuthē tō Iēsou·

paragraphs.text: this man went to Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded it to be given up.
paragraphs.original: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. τότε ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐκέλευσεν ἀποδοθῆναι.
paragraphs.translit: houtos proselthōn tō Pilatō ētēsato to sōma tou Iēsou. tote ho Pilatos ekeleusen apodothēnai.

paragraphs.text: And Joseph took the body, and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβὼν τὸ σῶμα ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι καθαρᾷ,
paragraphs.translit: kai labōn to sōma ho Iōsēph enetylixen auto sindoni kathara,

paragraphs.text: and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, and departed.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸ ἐν τῷ καινῷ αὐτοῦ μνημείῳ ὃ ἐλατόμησεν ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ, καὶ προσκυλίσας λίθον μέγαν τῇ θύρᾳ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ethēken auto en tō kainō autou mnēmeiō ho elatomēsen en tē petra, kai proskylisas lithon megan tē thyra tou mnēmeiou apēlthen.

paragraphs.text: And Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία καθήμεναι ἀπέναντι τοῦ τάφου.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de ekei Mariam hē Magdalēnē kai hē allē Maria kathēmenai apenanti tou taphou.

paragraphs.text: Now on the morrow, which is [the day] after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together unto Pilate,
paragraphs.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον, ἥτις ἐστὶν μετὰ τὴν παρασκευήν, συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς Πιλᾶτον
paragraphs.translit: Tē de epaurion, hētis estin meta tēn paraskeuēn, synēchthēsan hoi archiereis kai hoi Pharisaioi pros Pilaton

paragraphs.text: saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said while he was yet alive, After three days I rise again.
paragraphs.original: λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐμνήσθημεν ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὁ πλάνος εἶπεν ἔτι ζῶν· Μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγείρομαι·
paragraphs.translit: legontes· Kyrie, emnēsthēmen hoti ekeinos ho planos eipen eti zōn· Meta treis hēmeras egeiromai·

paragraphs.text: Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest haply his disciples come and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: and the last error will be worse than the first.
paragraphs.original: κέλευσον οὖν ἀσφαλισθῆναι τὸν τάφον ἕως τῆς τρίτης ἡμέρας, μήποτε ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κλέψωσιν αὐτὸν καὶ εἴπωσιν τῷ λαῷ· Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἔσται ἡ ἐσχάτη πλάνη χείρων τῆς πρώτης.
paragraphs.translit: keleuson oun asphalisthēnai ton taphon heōs tēs tritēs hēmeras, mēpote elthontes hoi mathētai autou klepsōsin auton kai eipōsin tō laō· Ēgerthē apo tōn nekrōn, kai estai hē eschatē planē cheirōn tēs prōtēs.

paragraphs.text: Pilate said unto them, Ye have a guard: go, make it [as] sure as ye can.
paragraphs.original: ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἔχετε κουστωδίαν· ὑπάγετε ἀσφαλίσασθε ὡς οἴδατε.
paragraphs.translit: ephē autois ho Pilatos· Echete koustōdian· hypagete asphalisasthe hōs oidate.

paragraphs.text: So they went, and made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone, the guard being with them.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ πορευθέντες ἠσφαλίσαντο τὸν τάφον σφραγίσαντες τὸν λίθον μετὰ τῆς κουστωδίας.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de poreuthentes ēsphalisanto ton taphon sphragisantes ton lithon meta tēs koustōdias.
